item.title: Suncoast Credit Union announces merger, would grow to over $21B
item.description: The largest credit union in Florida is about to get bigger: Tampa-based Suncoast Credit Union, with $19.68 billion in assets, announced a merger Friday with Launch Credit Union, based in Brevard County. Launch, serving Brevard and Volusia counties out of its Merritt Island headquarters, has more than $1.43 billion in assets. item.title: 7 in region make Forbes’ Best Large Employers list
item.description: Forbes released its 2026 “Best Large Employers” list this week, and it includes a handful of organizations from the region. Among them are three publicly traded companies, two health care systems, a university and a grocer.To qualify for the ranking, Forbes partnered with research firm Statista to analyze surveys from workers at organizations with more than 5,000 employees. item.title: National homebuilder buys 130 lots in Lakeland
item.description: An Atlanta-based homebuilder known for building communities for the “move-up buyer” announced Friday it has acquired 130 homesites inside Lakeland’s Hawthorne Ranch master-planned community. PulteGroup Inc. purchased finished lots ready for construction to begin immediately on new homes, the company says in a release, marking Pulte Homes' first residential development in the city of Lakeland and, the company says, an important step in its long-term growth strategy across Polk County. item.description: Although Wendy’s hasn’t specified which of its 350 restaurants will close as part of a nationwide plan, the fast-food giant announced recently it’s opening two locations in Manatee County this month.A Parrish store on U.S. 301 and a Palmetto store on Moccasin Wallow Road will feature the company’s latest design and décor, according to a release from the developer of the two stores, CASTO, based in Columbus, Ohio. item.title: Marine salvage and diving firm opens regional HQ in Pasco
item.description: A Pasco County-based marine services provider specializing in vessel salvage and commercial diving, Isla Maritime, is expanding its operations after opening its new U.S. headquarters in Port Richey this month, according to the Pasco County Economic Development Council. The company purchased a 3,000-square-foot warehouse and office space at 6802 Commerce Ave. in Port Richey to serve as its permanent base on the Gulf Coast, according to a release.
